source.snippet: In Flow Builder when we Deactivate the flow, sometimes we are asked whether we want to: Deactivate and complete work, or Deactivate and cancel work. And for some flows this question is not asked. But I still haven't figured out exactly when this happens. My code is trying to imitate that behavior. To deactivate the flow I currently use the tooling API to set the activeVersionNumber of a flow definition to 0. And this deactivates the flow but does not replicate the UI behavior faithfully.

problem_statement: Salesforce developers automating flow lifecycle management via the Tooling API cannot reliably replicate the platform's own deactivation behavior (complete vs. cancel in-flight work), leading to silent data integrity risks and unpredictable outcomes in automated deployment pipelines.
target_segment: Salesforce developers and admins building automated deployment or DevOps pipelines for Salesforce orgs, typically at ISVs or consulting firms.
notes: Buyer context: Salesforce consultants and ISV developers bill hourly and lose money on undocumented platform quirks. A verified reference implementation, tested library, or documentation service for Salesforce Tooling API edge cases has a clear paying audience. Single post; signal strength kept at 2.
